title: Cohere Proposed Acquisition of AISLE (Terms Undisclosed) to Launch Cohere Cyber
description: Cohere announced on October 15, 2026 a proposed agreement (letter of intent) to acquire AISLE, the Prague-based company building autonomous AI systems that discover, validate and remediate previously unknown vulnerabilities in production software. AISLE, founded in 2024, reported more than 500 previously unknown vulnerabilities assigned CVEs across more than 100 codebases in its first year out of stealth - including all 12 vulnerabilities in OpenSSL’s January security release and 18 of the 24 CVEs in curl’s latest release. Financial terms were not disclosed. AISLE’s three founders will take Cohere leadership roles - Ondrej Vlcek as Senior Vice President of the newly formed Cohere Cyber, Jaya Baloo as Cohere’s Chief Information Security Officer, and Stanislav Fort as Vice President of AI Security inside Cohere’s core model research and training - and Cohere plans a substantial long-term investment in Prague as its global AI-cybersecurity center. The deal deepens Cohere’s European presence following its Reliant AI and Aleph Alpha acquisitions.

title: Anthropic & Broadcom $42.0 Billion Convertible Note Lending Deal & S-1 Prospectus
description: Anthropic's roughly 300-page S-1/IPO prospectus revealed that Broadcom agreed to lend Anthropic up to $42.0 billion structured via convertible notes to fund roughly one-third of Anthropic's five-year, $125.2 billion commitment to lease TPU computing capacity. Under this multi-layered vendor financing arrangement, Broadcom acts simultaneously as hardware designer, equipment lessor, and direct lender with equity conversion rights at IPO against Anthropic's $518 billion in total cloud commitments.

title: CoreWeave $4.2 Billion 2.875% Convertible Senior Notes due 2033 (Upsized, Full $500M Greenshoe)
description: CoreWeave upsized and completed a convertible notes offering in September 2026: announced at $3.0 billion, priced at $3.7 billion on September 18, 2026, and closed at $4.2 billion aggregate principal of 2.875% convertible senior notes due 2033 on September 22, 2026 after the initial purchasers exercised their $500 million option in full (Rule 144A; U.S. Bank Trust Company trustee; guaranteed on a senior unsecured basis by CoreWeave subsidiaries that guarantee its existing 9.25%/9.0%/9.75%/9.625%/8.5% senior notes and 1.75% converts due 2031/2032). Net proceeds were $4,137.0 million, of which ~$566.2 million funded capped call transactions with nine named bank counterparties (cap price $199.70, a 150% premium over the September 17 close of $79.88); the notes carry a ~$97.85 initial conversion price (a ~22.50% premium), mature April 1, 2033, and are CoreWeave’s cheapest coupon since its IPO - proceeds fund general corporate purposes.

title: Mistral AI €3 Billion Series D Funding Round at €21B+ Valuation
description: Mistral AI raised €3 billion in a Series D at a post-money valuation above €21 billion — per the company, the largest equity fundraising round ever completed by a European technology company. Samsung Electronics led, joined by co-leads Scaleup Europe Fund (managed by EQT) and existing investor PSG Equity; Advent, BlackRock-managed funds and the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg joined as new investors, and existing holders including ASML, Andreessen Horowitz, NVIDIA, Lightspeed, General Catalyst, DST Global, Index Ventures, Salesforce Ventures and Bpifrance participated. The round funds deeper frontier research, expanded infrastructure and accelerated international growth, nearly doubling the €11.7B valuation set by the ASML-led Series C a year earlier.

title: NVIDIA Agrees to Acquire Hugging Face for ~$12.93 Billion (Signed; Close Expected H1 2027)
description: On September 2, 2026 NVIDIA entered a definitive agreement to acquire Hugging Face, Inc. - the open-source AI platform hosting roughly 3 million models, a half-million datasets and 1 million applications used by over 18 million developers - for approximately $12.93 billion: about $11.9 billion payable to Hugging Face stockholders plus an equity-based retention program of up to about $1.0 billion for employees joining NVIDIA. Announced September 3, 2026 (NVIDIA Form 8-K; Jensen Huang blog), the deal is a massive software/platform bet on open AI models and NVIDIA's second-largest purchase ever, after the ~$20B Groq asset purchase in December 2025. NVIDIA committed publicly to keep Hugging Face an open platform: model makers and developers choose their models, frameworks, clouds and computing platforms, NVIDIA compute will not be required, and support for other silicon vendors continues. Hugging Face CEO Clément Delangue told CNBC the company approached Huang over the summer and a deal came together weeks later. Closing is expected in the first half of 2027, subject to regulatory approvals.

title: Stripe Agrees to Acquire OpenRouter, the AI Model Marketplace
description: Stripe announced on August 19, 2026 that it agreed to acquire OpenRouter, the largest AI model marketplace and inference gateway, routing 10+ trillion tokens daily across 400+ models and marketed by observers as \

title: Marvell Issues Google $12.2B Stock Warrant Tied to $120B Chip Purchases
description: Marvell and Google signed a commercial agreement on July 29, 2026 for custom silicon attaching to the TPU ecosystem (AI inference accelerators, storage/network/memory controllers, near-memory compute). On August 18, 2026 Marvell issued Google a warrant for up to 58,970,907 shares (~7% of Marvell) at $206.58 apiece, worth ~$12.2B at exercise: 1,360,867 shares vest quarterly over one year and the rest vests in 240 tranches of $500M of Custom Products revenue, i.e. up to $120B of chip purchases through FY2033. The warrant runs to August 18, 2033; MRVL shares rallied ~10% on the news.

title: Groq $350 Million Series A at a $3.5 Billion Valuation (Disruptive-Led, Planned NVIDIA Participation)
description: Groq LLC announced on August 17, 2026 a $350 million Series A led by Disruptive - whose CEO Alex Davis also serves as Groq’s Executive Chairman - with planned participation from NVIDIA, valuing the AI-inference-cloud company at $3.5 billion. Together with $650 million raised in June 2026, that brings recent funding to $1 billion. Groq operates 13 data centers across North America, Europe, the Middle East and Asia Pacific serving 6 million-plus developers and Fortune 500 enterprises, and expects to scale from 54 megawatts to 200+ megawatts in 2027; the company operates as an NVIDIA Cloud Partner deploying NVIDIA accelerated computing. The release headline states the round closed, while noting the fundraise is subject to customary closing conditions.

title: Databricks $5 Billion Strategic Funding Round at a $190 Billion Valuation (Coatue-Led)
description: Databricks closed a $5 billion strategic funding round at a $190 billion valuation, announced August 13, 2026 alongside >80% YoY growth and a $7 billion revenue run-rate in its Q2. The round was led by Coatue, along with Blackstone, MGX, accounts advised by T. Rowe Price Associates and T. Rowe Price Investment Management, and new investor Sixth Street Growth; other new investors included BOND, Clearlake Capital, Point72, Premji Invest and TPG, alongside existing investors including Andreessen Horowitz, Dragoneer, Fidelity, Franklin Templeton, GIC, Growth Equity at Goldman Sachs Alternatives, Insight Partners, J.P. Morgan Private Capital, Morgan Stanley Investment Management, NEA, Ontario Teachers’ Pension Plan, Temasek, Thrive Capital and WCM. Capital targets Lakebase (>$100M run-rate), Genie and Unity AI Gateway for enterprise AI agents; Coatue co-founder Thomas Laffont said Coatue has been an investor since 2019 and is "proud to lead this round."

title: NVIDIA Investment in Safe Superintelligence (Reported $5B) Alongside Vera Rubin Partnership
description: On July 27, 2026, Safe Superintelligence (SSI) and NVIDIA announced a long-term strategic partnership: NVIDIA made an investment in SSI (amount not disclosed by either company) and will give SSI access to best-in-class Vera Rubin systems to increase its compute by an order of magnitude, with the two companies also collaborating on the technical advancement of NVIDIA's current and future compute platforms. Bloomberg first reported the investment at $5 billion, corroborated by Reuters (person briefed on the deal); SSI's ~$32 billion valuation is media-reported. SSI - which ships no product - said the investment will let it 10x its compute within 12 months, and the joint release lists its existing investors as Andreessen Horowitz, DST Global, Greenoaks and Sequoia Capital.

title: SpaceX Completes $60.0 Billion All-Stock Acquisition of Anysphere (Cursor)
description: Space Exploration Technologies Corp. (SpaceX), its wholly owned merger subsidiary X67 Inc., and Anysphere, Inc. (Cursor) signed an Agreement and Plan of Merger on June 16, 2026, and the merger became effective August 14, 2026. Cursor's common and preferred shares converted into 389,289,254 SpaceX Class A shares based on an implied equity value of Cursor of $60.0 billion at the volume-weighted average closing price of SpaceX Class A stock over the seven trading days preceding closing, plus 1,752,426 additional shares for vested Cursor RSUs; unvested RSUs and options were assumed and converted into roughly 29.1 million SpaceX RSUs and 44.4 million options. Cursor became a wholly owned SpaceX subsidiary - which Bloomberg called the largest startup acquisition on record and a key part of Elon Musk's bid to gain ground on Anthropic and OpenAI in AI coding - and Cursor's own blog confirmed "Cursor is now a part of SpaceX" on completion day.

title: Supermicro $5B Underwritten Equity Package ($1.25B Common + $3.75B Mandatory Converts)
description: Supermicro announced concurrent equity financings on June 9, 2026 to fund ~$39B of AI server component orders, and priced them on June 11: 45,454,545 common shares at $27.50 ($1.25B gross) plus 75,000,000 depositary shares at $50 ($3.75B gross) representing 7% Series A mandatory convertible preferred auto-converting ~June 2029 (listed SMCIP). The common leg closed June 12 and the depositary leg June 15, 2026, for ~$4.9B net. J.P. Morgan, Goldman Sachs and Citigroup acted as lead joint bookrunners; a separate $1.25B ATM program with the same banks was also signed.

title: Alphabet ~$85B Equity Capital Raise with $10B Berkshire Cornerstone
description: Alphabet announced a proposed $80 billion equity capital raise on June 1, 2026 to fund AI infrastructure: a $10 billion direct stock purchase by Berkshire Hathaway, a $30 billion underwritten offering tranche, and ~$40 billion of staggered open-market sales. Alphabet said the underwritten tranche was oversubscribed with ~$35 billion priced and allocated, lifting the expected total to ~$85B. Proceeds back record AI capex guided at $180-190B for 2026; Alphabet shares slipped only ~1-2% on a >$4.5T market cap.

title: Anthropic $65 Billion Series H Funding Round at $965 Billion Post-Money Valuation
description: Anthropic raised $65 billion in a Series H at a $965 billion post-money valuation — surpassing OpenAI's $852B as the most valuable AI startup — led by Altimeter Capital, Dragoneer, Greenoaks and Sequoia Capital, and co-led by Capital Group, Coatue, D1 Capital Partners, GIC, ICONIQ and XN. The round includes $15 billion of previously committed hyperscaler investments ($5 billion from Amazon) and adds strategic infrastructure partners Micron, Samsung and SK hynix; MGX, Blackstone, Brookfield, D.E. Shaw Ventures, DST Global, Fidelity, General Catalyst, Jane Street, Lightspeed, T. Rowe Price and Temasek also participated. Anthropic's run-rate revenue crossed $47 billion in May 2026; funding advances safety and interpretability research, compute expansion (new agreements with Amazon for up to 5 GW, Google/Broadcom for 5 GW of TPU capacity, and SpaceX for Colossus GPU access), and product scaling.

title: Anduril $5 Billion Series H Funding Round at $61 Billion Valuation
description: Anduril Industries raised $5 billion in a Series H led by Thrive Capital and Andreessen Horowitz, doubling its valuation to $61 billion from the $30.5 billion set by its June 2025 Founders Fund-led Series G ($2.5B with a $1B Founders Fund check). Co-founder CEO Brian Schimpf said revenue more than doubled to $2.2 billion in 2025; proceeds fund manufacturing capacity, R&D, and the infrastructure required to build and field advanced defense systems at scale.

title: Meta-CoreWeave $21B AI Cloud Capacity Expansion (2026)
description: Expansion of the Meta-CoreWeave relationship recorded separately from the September 2025 $14.2B order form (20000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000115): per CoreWeave’s Form 8-K, Meta entered a new order form on March 31, 2026 under the same December 2023 master services agreement, initially committing approximately $21 billion for dedicated AI cloud capacity — inclusive of new capacity through December 20, 2032 and the exercise of an existing option for additional capacity through April 10, 2032. The dedicated capacity spans multiple locations and includes some of the first deployments of the NVIDIA Vera Rubin platform, scaling Meta’s AI inference workloads.

title: OpenAI $122 Billion Funding Round at $852 Billion Post-Money Valuation
description: OpenAI closed its latest funding round with $122 billion in committed capital at an $852 billion post-money valuation — the largest private financing in history — after announcing $110 billion at a $730 billion pre-money valuation on February 27, 2026. The round was anchored by strategic partners Amazon ($50B, of which $35B is contingent on an IPO or reaching AGI), NVIDIA ($30B) and SoftBank ($30B), with continued participation from Microsoft; SoftBank co-led alongside Andreessen Horowitz, D. E. Shaw Ventures, MGX, TPG and accounts advised by T. Rowe Price Associates. OpenAI extended participation to individual investors through bank channels for the first time, raising $3 billion. The expanded NVIDIA collaboration includes 3 GW of dedicated inference and 2 GW of Vera Rubin training capacity, and the Amazon partnership expands the $38B AWS compute deal by $100B with AWS as exclusive third-party cloud distributor for OpenAI Frontier.

title: CoreWeave $8.5 Billion Investment-Grade Delayed Draw Term Loan (DDTL 4.0)
description: CoreWeave secured a landmark $8.5 billion investment-grade rated term loan facility anchored by Blackstone Credit & Insurance alongside JPMorgan, Morgan Stanley, and MUFG. Rated A3 by Moodys, this transaction marked the worlds first investment-grade credit facility secured by enterprise GPU compute contracts and high-performance hardware.

title: Nebius $12B Dedicated AI Capacity Agreement with Meta
description: Nebius will provide Meta with $12B of dedicated AI capacity over five years starting early 2027, with up to $15B of additional optional capacity bringing the total envelope to about $27B.

title: Nebius Group $2.0 Billion Strategic Equity Investment from NVIDIA
description: NVIDIA invested $2.0 billion in Nebius Group N.V. via private placement of Class A ordinary shares, solidifying a strategic hyperscale pact to co-deploy over 5 gigawatts of computing capacity by 2030 powered by NVIDIA Rubin, Vera CPUs, and BlueField architecture.

title: Anthropic $30 Billion Series G Funding Round at $380 Billion Valuation
description: Anthropic raised $30 billion in a Series G at a $380 billion post-money valuation, led by GIC and Coatue and co-led by D. E. Shaw Ventures, Dragoneer, Founders Fund, ICONIQ and MGX, with participation from Accel, Altimeter, Blackstone, Fidelity, General Catalyst, Jane Street, Lightspeed, QIA, Sequoia, Temasek, TPG and others. The round includes a portion of the previously announced Microsoft (up to $5B) and NVIDIA (up to $10B) investment commitments. CNBC called it the second-biggest private tech financing on record at announcement, after OpenAI's 2025 raise; OpenAI's $122B round (March 2026) and Anthropic's own $65B Series H (May 2026) have since surpassed it. Proceeds fund frontier research, product development, and infrastructure expansion behind Claude.

title: SoftBank Group $10 Billion Strategic Capital Tranche in OpenAI
description: SoftBank Group completed an initial $10 billion direct equity funding tranche into OpenAI as part of Masayoshi Son broader $30 billion multi-stage commitment to accelerate American supercomputing, frontier intelligence scaling, and autonomous AI systems.

title: SpaceX Acquires xAI in All-Stock ~$1.25T Merger (Signed January 31, 2026; Closed February 2, 2026)
description: Elon Musk combined his rocket, satellite-internet and AI empires: SpaceX signed an Agreement and Plan of Merger and Reorganization with X.AI Holdings Corp. (xAI) on January 31, 2026 and completed the all-stock merger on February 2, 2026, announced the same day - making xAI (developer of Grok and owner of the X social platform following the 2025 xAI-X merger) a wholly owned SpaceX subsidiary through a two-step Nevada merger (K2 Merger Sub Inc., then K2 Merger Sub 2 LLC). The transaction valued xAI at approximately $250 billion within a combined company valued around $1 trillion, with the combined entity reported at roughly $1.25 trillion ahead of a planned IPO (Reuters, citing Bloomberg, called it the biggest M&A transaction of all time), positioning the combination to fund Musk's ambitions for data centers in space. The structure was an intended tax-free reorganization (IRC Section 368) that avoided repayment triggers on xAI's debt and shielded SpaceX from xAI legal liabilities, per Reuters' follow-up on completed-deal mechanics. Musk framed the merger as \

title: Vistra & Meta 20-Year 2,609 MW Nuclear Power Agreements & Capacity Uprates
description: Vistra Corp entered into landmark 20-year power purchase agreements with Meta Platforms covering 2,609 MW of carbon-free nuclear energy and capacity from the Perry, Davis-Besse, and Beaver Valley nuclear plants, including 433 MW of newly committed power uprates.

title: xAI $20 Billion Series E Funding Round
description: xAI completed its upsized $20 billion Series E funding round, exceeding the original $15 billion target. Valor Equity Partners, StepStone Group, Fidelity Management & Research Company, Qatar Investment Authority, MGX and Baron Capital Group participated, with NVIDIA and Cisco Investments joining as strategic investors (NVIDIA had planned as much as $2B per Bloomberg). Bloomberg reported during the round a planned split of roughly $7.5B of equity plus as much as $12.5B of SPV debt to purchase NVIDIA processors leased back to xAI for five years; the company did not break out portions or confirm a valuation, with press reports citing roughly $230B. The release cites Colossus I and II ending 2025 with over one million H100 GPU equivalents and says proceeds accelerate infrastructure buildout, product deployment and research, with Grok 5 in training.

title: NVIDIA’s ~$20 Billion License-and-Hire Deal with Groq
description: NVIDIA struck its largest deal ever in late December 2025: a roughly $20 billion package that grants it a non-exclusive license to rival inference-chip maker Groq’s Language Processing Unit (LPU) technology, with Groq founder/CEO Jonathan Ross, president Sunny Madra and a large part of the engineering team joining NVIDIA to scale the licensed technology inside NVIDIA’s AI factory architecture. It is not an equity acquisition: Groq continues as an independent company under new CEO Simon Edwards and GroqCloud keeps operating. NVIDIA’s regulatory-filing disclosures later detailed $13 billion of cash consideration at closing plus $4 billion payable within a year (approx. $17 billion) and a $2.5 billion developed-technology intangible.

title: Databricks Series L Completes: ~$5B Equity at a $134B Valuation with Microsoft and JPMorganChase SIG in Additional Close
description: Databricks announced on December 16, 2025 that it was raising a >$4 billion Series L at a $134 billion valuation (led by Insight Partners, Fidelity Management & Research Company and J.P. Morgan Asset Management, with a16z, BlackRock, Blackstone, Coatue, GIC, MGX, NEA, Ontario Teachers’, Temasek, Thrive and others participating). On February 9, 2026 the company announced it was completing investments in excess of $7 billion - comprising ~$5B of equity financing at the $134 billion valuation plus ~$2B of additional debt capacity - after an additional close that brought in Microsoft, JPMorganChase (via its Security and Resiliency Initiative’s newly formed Strategic Investment Group), Glade Brook Capital, Growth Equity at Goldman Sachs Alternatives, Morgan Stanley, funds affiliated with Neuberger, Qatar Investment Authority and funds associated with UBS. The capital targets Lakebase, Genie and Agent Bricks, AI research, strategic acquisitions and employee liquidity; Databricks also crossed a $5.4 billion revenue run-rate growing >65% YoY in Q4.

title: CoreWeave $2.5875B Convertible Senior Notes (Upsized, Dec 2025)
description: CoreWeave announced a $2B convertible notes offering on December 8, 2025, priced an upsized $2.25B tranche on December 9 (1.75% coupon due 2031, conversion price ~$107.80, a 25% premium to $86.24), and closed $2,587,500,000 on December 11, 2025 after initial purchasers exercised the $337.5M greenshoe in full. Net proceeds were ~$2,542.2M for general corporate purposes; ~$340M funded capped-call hedges (cap $215.60) with seven named bank counterparties including Morgan Stanley and Goldman Sachs.

title: NVIDIA $2 Billion Purchase of Synopsys Common Stock at $414.79/Share
description: On December 1, 2025, Synopsys entered into a Securities Purchase Agreement under which NVIDIA purchased 4,821,717 shares of Synopsys common stock at $414.79 per share for an aggregate $2 billion in cash, announced alongside an expanded multi-year strategic partnership to bring NVIDIA CUDA GPU-accelerated computing into Synopsys' EDA and simulation platform - GPU-accelerated engineering and marketing collaboration spanning semiconductors, aerospace, automotive and industrial design, with cloud access for GPU-accelerated engineering solutions. Synopsys' 8-K (Item 3.02) records the completed same-day purchase; the price sat at a slight discount to the prior week's close, and SNPS shares rose on the announcement.

title: Anthropic $30B Microsoft Azure Compute Commitment
description: On November 18, 2025, Microsoft, NVIDIA, and Anthropic announced strategic partnerships under which Anthropic committed to purchase $30 billion of Azure compute capacity, with additional compute contracted up to one gigawatt on NVIDIA Grace Blackwell and Vera Rubin systems, scaling Claude on Azure. Microsoft committed up to $5 billion and NVIDIA up to $10 billion in Anthropic investments as part of the same three-way announcement (tracked separately).

title: Microsoft Up to $5 Billion Investment Commitment in Anthropic
description: On November 18, 2025, Microsoft and Anthropic announced an expanded partnership bringing Claude to Microsoft Foundry and the Copilot family, with Anthropic committing to purchase $30 billion of Azure compute capacity (plus up to one additional gigawatt) powered by NVIDIA systems. As part of the same three-way announcement, Microsoft committed to invest up to $5 billion in Anthropic, alongside NVIDIA up to $10 billion. Anthropic was valued in the range of ~$350 billion in connection with the deal (CNBC); Microsoft later recorded a ~$3.2B mark-up gain on its Anthropic holding in its July 2026 results (TechCrunch), consistent with deployment of the commitment.

title: NVIDIA Up to $10 Billion Investment Commitment in Anthropic
description: On November 18, 2025, NVIDIA and Anthropic announced a deep technology partnership: Anthropic adopting NVIDIA architectures (initially up to one gigawatt of Grace Blackwell and Vera Rubin systems) and committing to purchase $30 billion of Microsoft Azure compute powered by NVIDIA, while NVIDIA committed to invest up to $10 billion in Anthropic alongside Microsoft. Anthropic was valued in the range of ~$350 billion in connection with the deal (CNBC). Deployment of the phased investment was not yet evidenced as completed in primary filings at review time.

title: Amazon $15 Billion US Bond Offering for AI Infrastructure
description: Amazon raised $15 billion in its first US dollar bond sale in three years on November 17, 2025, via six-part investment-grade notes (including a 40-year tranche) that topped the initial $12 billion target with about $80 billion of peak demand; proceeds support business investments including AI data center and chip capex, debt maturities, and buybacks. Goldman Sachs, JPMorgan Chase, and Morgan Stanley managed the sale.

title: Anysphere (Cursor) $2.3 Billion Series D at $29.3 Billion Post-Money Valuation
description: Anysphere, maker of the AI coding platform Cursor, announced the successful closing of its $2.3 billion Series D at a $29.3 billion post-money valuation on November 13, 2025, with continued commitment from existing investors Thrive, a16z, Accel and DST and new investment from Coatue, NVIDIA and Google. The company said it had exceeded $1 billion in annualized revenue and grown to more than 300 engineers, researchers, designers and operators across San Francisco and New York. CNBC and Bloomberg independently reported the round; less than a year later, SpaceX completed its $60.0 billion acquisition of Anysphere (August 14, 2026).

title: Alphabet $25 Billion Global Bond Sale for AI Capex
description: Alphabet sold approximately $25 billion of bonds in early November 2025 — $17.5 billion of eight-part US dollar notes (3- to 50-year) plus EUR 6.5 billion of euro notes — drawing about $90 billion of USD orders; proceeds support record AI-driven cloud capital expenditures guided at $91-93 billion for 2025. Morgan Stanley was among the lead managers of the US dollar offering alongside Goldman Sachs, HSBC, JPMorgan, Bank of America, Citigroup, and Wells Fargo.

title: OpenAI $38B Seven-Year AWS Cloud Compute Contract
description: OpenAI signed a seven-year, $38 billion agreement to run core AI workloads on Amazon Web Services, accessing hundreds of thousands of NVIDIA GPUs (GB200/GB300 via EC2 UltraServers) with all initial capacity targeted for deployment before end of 2026. The deal marks OpenAI’s first major AWS partnership following the end of Microsoft’s exclusive cloud arrangement.

title: Meta $30 Billion Senior Notes Offering for AI Infrastructure
description: Meta Platforms priced a $30 billion six-part senior notes offering (tranches due 2030-2065) on October 30, 2025, the biggest US high-grade bond sale of the year with a reported $125 billion record order book; net proceeds of about $29.9 billion were designated for general corporate purposes as Meta funds AI infrastructure expansion. Citigroup and Morgan Stanley acted as joint book-running managers.

title: AWS Project Rainier for Anthropic: ~500K Trainium2 Chips Operational, Scaling to More Than 1M
description: Project Rainier - the EC2 UltraCluster of Trainium2 UltraServers AWS built for Anthropic - came fully operational on or around October 29, 2025, less than a year after it was first announced: nearly half a million AWS-designed Trainium2 chips across multiple U.S. data centers (including St. Joseph County, Indiana) provide more than five times the compute power Anthropic used to train its previous models, and Anthropic is actively training and running Claude on it, with more than 1 million Trainium2 chips expected by the end of 2025. AWS says Rainier’s cumulative infrastructure is 70% larger than any other AI computing platform in its history. Anthropic remains multi-cloud - it also holds the ~$38B AWS platform commitment (deal ...074) plus Google TPU capacity recorded elsewhere in the ledger - so this record covers the dedicated Rainier build-out, distinct from those agreements.

title: Microsoft-OpenAI $250B Incremental Azure Commitment
description: As part of the definitive next-phase partnership announced October 28, 2025 alongside OpenAI’s recapitalization into a public benefit corporation, OpenAI contracted to purchase an incremental $250 billion of Microsoft Azure services. Microsoft simultaneously gave up its right of first refusal to be OpenAI’s compute provider, letting OpenAI buy capacity elsewhere while Azure remains its primary cloud.

title: Anthropic-Google Cloud TPU Expansion (Up to 1M TPUs)
description: Jointly announced October 23, 2025: Anthropic will expand its use of Google Cloud with access to up to one million TPUs plus additional Google Cloud services to train and serve the next generations of Claude — the largest expansion of Anthropic’s TPU usage to date. Both companies described the expansion as worth tens of billions of dollars and expected to bring well over a gigawatt of capacity online in 2026. No specific dollar figure was disclosed, so no cash value is recorded.

title: Meta-Blue Owl $27B Hyperion Data Center Joint Venture
description: Meta closed an approximately $27B joint venture with Blue Owl Capital funds to finance the Hyperion AI data center campus in Richland Parish, Louisiana. Early August 2025 reporting described a $29B package of roughly $26B PIMCO-arranged debt plus $3B Blue Owl equity; the closed JV covers about $27B of development.

title: NextEra Energy & Google 25-Year 615 MW Duane Arnold Nuclear Plant Restart PPA
description: NextEra Energy and Google signed a 25-year strategic agreement to recommission and restart the 615-megawatt Duane Arnold Energy Center in Iowa, delivering 24/7 carbon-free baseload nuclear electricity directly to support Google cloud and AI computing facilities across the Midwest.

title: OpenAI-Broadcom 10 GW Custom AI Accelerator Collaboration
description: OpenAI and Broadcom announced a multi-year collaboration for 10 gigawatts of OpenAI-designed custom AI accelerators with Broadcom Ethernet networking, signing a term sheet for rack deployment starting H2 2026 through end of 2029. Financial terms were not disclosed.

title: xAI ~$7.5B SPV Equity Portion of ~$20B Colossus 2 GPU Financing (NVIDIA up to $2B, Valor-led)
description: Bloomberg reported on October 7-8, 2025 (relayed by Reuters) that Elon Musk’s xAI had expanded its ongoing financing to ~$20 billion for its Colossus 2 data center in Memphis through a special purpose vehicle that purchases NVIDIA processors and leases them back to xAI for five years. The package splits into roughly $7.5 billion of equity and as much as $12.5 billion of SPV debt; NVIDIA is investing as much as $2 billion in the equity portion, and Valor Equity Partners is leading the equity leg. The raise was reported as ongoing and was not confirmed by the company at the time; it is distinct from the company-confirmed upsized $20B Series E announced January 6, 2026.

title: xAI up to $12.5B SPV GPU-Collateralized Debt for Colossus 2 (Apollo, Diameter Participating)
description: As part of the ~$20 billion financing package Bloomberg reported on October 7-8, 2025 (relayed by Reuters), up to $12.5 billion of debt is being raised through a special purpose vehicle that purchases NVIDIA processors and leases them to xAI for five years for its Colossus 2 project in Memphis. The loan is backed by the GPUs rather than the company’s credit, letting Wall Street financiers recoup their investment through the hardware — a structure Bloomberg flagged as a potential playbook for capital-intensive AI ventures. Apollo Global Management and Diameter Capital Partners were reported participating in the debt raise; the financing remained in progress and unconfirmed by the company at the time of reporting.

title: AMD-OpenAI 6 GW Strategic GPU Partnership with Share Warrants
description: AMD and OpenAI signed a definitive multi-year agreement for OpenAI to deploy 6 gigawatts of AMD Instinct GPUs across multiple generations, starting with a 1 GW MI450 rollout in H2 2026. AMD issued OpenAI a warrant for up to 160 million shares (~10%) at $0.01 vesting on deployment and share-price milestones. No hard dollar purchase figure was disclosed.

title: Meta-CoreWeave $14.2B AI Cloud Capacity Contract
description: CoreWeave disclosed via Form 8-K that Meta entered a new order form on September 25, 2025 under its December 2023 master services agreement, committing up to approximately $14.2 billion for dedicated AI cloud capacity through December 14, 2031, with the option to materially expand its commitment through 2032. The agreement provides Meta access to NVIDIA GB300 systems and lets CoreWeave fill data center capacity beyond its largest customer, Microsoft.

title: Vistra & Amazon 20-Year 1,200 MW Comanche Peak Nuclear Power Agreement
description: Vistra signed a 20-year power purchase agreement with Amazon Web Services for up to 1,200 MW of carbon-free electricity generated from the Comanche Peak nuclear power plant in Texas, with options for an additional 20-year extension.

title: Google $1.4B Backstop of Fluidstack Leases at Cipher Barber Lake for ~5.4% Warrants (Later $1.73B)
description: Cipher Mining signed a 10-year HPC colocation lease with Fluidstack USA II at its Barber Lake site in Colorado City, Texas, delivering 168 MW of critical IT load (up to 244 MW gross) for ~$3.0B of contracted revenue over the initial term (~$7B if two five-year extensions are exercised). Google LLC agreed to backstop $1.4B of Fluidstack’s lease obligations to support project-related debt financing under a Recognition Agreement among Cipher Barber Lake LLC, Fluidstack and Google, receiving warrants for 24,178,576 Cipher shares at $0.01 exercise (~5.4% pro forma equity, expiring September 24, 2030); Cipher booked the warrants at a $544.5M fair value in its 10-Q. On November 20, 2025 the partnership was expanded — Fluidstack to lease the full 300 MW of Barber Lake with ~$830M of added contracted revenue (~$3.8B partnership total over the initial term) — and Google’s backstop rose by $333M to $1.73B via Amended and Restated Recognition and Warrant Agreements.

title: Nscale $1.1B Series B Led by Aker ASA
description: Nscale raised an oversubscribed $1.1 billion Series B, the largest in UK and European history, led by Aker ASA with a $285 million cash-plus-assets commitment for a 9.3% fully diluted stake. Other participants included Sandton Capital, Blue Owl Managed Funds, Dell, Fidelity, G Squared, Nokia, NVIDIA, Point72, and T.Capital; proceeds accelerate Nscale AI infrastructure rollout across Europe, North America, and the Middle East.

title: OpenAI-CoreWeave $6.5B Compute Expansion (Total ~$22.4B)
description: Expansion of the OpenAI-CoreWeave base contract recorded as 20000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000061 ($11.9B, March 2025): per CoreWeave’s Form 8-K, OpenAI entered a new order form on September 23, 2025 under the May 8, 2025 master services agreement, committing to pay up to approximately $6.5 billion through May 31, 2031 for cloud computing capacity to train its most advanced next-generation models. Together with the March 2025 base contract and a May 2025 expansion of up to $4 billion, total OpenAI-CoreWeave contract value reached approximately $22.4 billion.

title: Oracle $18 Billion Investment-Grade Senior Notes Offering
description: Oracle priced an $18 billion six-part investment-grade senior notes offering (tranches due 2030-2065) on September 24, 2025, the market’s second-largest deal of the year with roughly $88-90 billion of orders; net proceeds of about $17.9 billion were earmarked for general corporate purposes including capital expenditures on cloud infrastructure for AI demand. J.P. Morgan Securities LLC acted as a joint book-running manager alongside BofA Securities, Citigroup, Deutsche Bank, Goldman Sachs, and HSBC.

title: NVIDIA-OpenAI Up-to-$100B Letter of Intent for 10 GW Deployment
description: NVIDIA and OpenAI signed a non-binding letter of intent for at least 10 gigawatts of NVIDIA systems (starting with Vera Rubin in H2 2026), with NVIDIA intending to invest up to $100B progressively as each gigawatt deploys. The arrangement was never finalized: WSJ reporting relayed by Reuters in January 2026 described the megadeal as stalled/on ice, and NVIDIA’s CEO later stated the $100B figure was never a firm commitment.

title: Meta-Oracle ~$20B Multi-Year AI Cloud Contract
description: Oracle and Meta struck a multi-year cloud computing deal worth about $20 billion under which Oracle provides Meta computing capacity for training and deploying AI models, in addition to Meta’s existing cloud providers. Bloomberg first reported the talks on September 19, 2025, and Oracle confirmed the deal’s existence on October 16, 2025, when CEO Clay Magouyrk said Meta was one of four customers behind $65 billion of new OCI commitments contracted in 30 days. The commitment contributed to Oracle’s RPO surge, including Q2 FY26 growth Oracle attributed to "new commitments from Meta, NVIDIA, and others."

title: NVIDIA $5 Billion Equity Investment in Intel at $23.28/Share
description: NVIDIA announced a collaboration with Intel on September 18, 2025 to jointly develop multiple generations of custom data center and PC products: Intel-built NVIDIA-custom x86 CPUs integrated into NVIDIA AI infrastructure platforms, and x86 system-on-chips with NVIDIA RTX GPU chiplets. Alongside the product agreement, NVIDIA committed to invest $5 billion in newly issued Intel common stock at $23.28 per share (~214.8M shares). Intel completed the issuance and sale on December 26, 2025 after regulatory clearance, taking NVIDIA to roughly a 4% equity stake.

title: NVIDIA Pays Reported >$900M to License Enfabrica Technology and Hire Its CEO
description: NVIDIA spent more than $900 million in a cash-and-stock package to license the technology of networking-silicon startup Enfabrica and hire its CEO Rochan Sankar plus other employees, per CNBC (two people familiar with the arrangement). The deal, which closed the week before the September 18, 2025 report, is a license-plus-hire rather than an equity acquisition: Enfabrica’s fabric technology - which can tie roughly 100,000 AI accelerators into a single computer while cutting memory costs - is being folded into NVIDIA’s AI-factory networking stack. NVIDIA had already backed Enfabrica’s $125M Series B in 2023.

title: Figure Series C Exceeds $1 Billion at $39 Billion Post-Money Valuation
description: Figure, the AI robotics company developing autonomous general-purpose humanoid robots, announced on September 16, 2025 that it had exceeded more than $1 billion in committed capital through its Series C financing round at a $39 billion post-money valuation. The round was led by Parkway Venture Capital with significant investment from Brookfield Asset Management, NVIDIA, Macquarie Capital, Intel Capital, Align Ventures, Tamarack Global, LG Technology Ventures, Salesforce, T-Mobile Ventures and Qualcomm Ventures. The capital targets three fronts - scaling the Helix embodied-AI platform, robot training infrastructure and advanced real-world data collection - and BotQ volume manufacturing; TechCrunch called it Figure's largest round yet, bringing total funding to nearly $2 billion since its 2022 founding.

title: Anthropic $13 Billion Series F Financing Round at $183 Billion Valuation
description: Anthropic secured $13 billion in a landmark Series F funding round led by ICONIQ Capital, Fidelity Management & Research, and Lightspeed Venture Partners at a $183 billion post-money valuation, funding massive frontier compute capacity and expansion of Claude across enterprise cloud platforms.

title: OpenAI-Oracle $300B Five-Year Stargate Compute Contract
description: OpenAI signed a contract to purchase roughly $300 billion of computing power from Oracle over about five years beginning in 2027, first reported by WSJ on September 10, 2025, supplying the 4.5 GW of additional Stargate capacity agreed in July. OpenAI subsequently confirmed on the record that its Oracle partnership "exceeds $300 billion... over the next five years." This record tracks the reported contract value; the underlying capacity agreements are tracked separately as the June 2025 gigawatt-scale OCI agreement and the July 2025 4.5 GW Stargate expansion.

title: Mistral AI €1.7 Billion Series C at €11.7B Valuation
description: Mistral AI raised €1.7 billion in a Series C at an €11.7 billion post-money valuation led by ASML (€1.3B, ~11% stake) with NVIDIA, Andreessen Horowitz, DST Global, General Catalyst and others participating, alongside a long-term ASML strategic partnership.

title: Databricks $1 Billion Series K at Over $100B Valuation
description: Databricks closed a $1 billion Series K funding round at a valuation over $100 billion, co-led by existing investors Andreessen Horowitz, Insight Partners, MGX, Thrive Capital and WCM Investment Management, on the back of a $4 billion revenue run-rate and $1 billion AI revenue run-rate.

title: Nebius $17.4B AI Infrastructure Agreement with Microsoft
description: Nebius agreed to supply Microsoft with AI infrastructure worth $17.4B through 2031, with optional expansion bringing total potential contract value to $19.4B.

title: Meta-Google Cloud $10B+ Six-Year Compute Deal
description: Meta struck a six-year cloud computing deal with Google worth more than $10 billion, mainly for AI infrastructure, per reporting in August 2025. Meta will use Google Cloud for servers, storage, networking and other services, with access to GPUs and TPUs to scale AI workloads, as Meta’s 2025 capex guidance climbed to as high as $72 billion.

title: SoftBank $2 Billion Equity Investment in Intel at $23.00/Share
description: SoftBank Group and Intel announced a definitive securities purchase agreement on August 18, 2025 under which SoftBank invested $2 billion in newly issued Intel common stock at $23.00 per share (86,956,522 shares). Both CEOs framed the investment as deepening commitment to US semiconductor manufacturing. The issuance and sale completed on September 26, 2025; Reuters/LSEG noted SoftBank would become Intel roughly sixth-largest shareholder.

title: OpenAI $6.6 Billion Employee Secondary Share Sale at a $500 Billion Valuation
description: OpenAI current and former employees sold approximately $6.6 billion of existing shares to a consortium of investors including SoftBank, Thrive Capital, Dragoneer Investment Group, Abu Dhabi's MGX and T. Rowe Price, completing on October 2, 2025 at a $500 billion valuation that made OpenAI the world's most valuable private company. The sale fell short of the over $10 billion (reported as $10.3 billion) of stock OpenAI had authorized for the secondary - which insiders read as a sign of employee confidence and continued investor demand - and, as a pure secondary, OpenAI itself raised no new primary capital. Bloomberg first reported the buyer lineup on August 15, 2025, and the sale adds to SoftBank's position from OpenAI's earlier $40 billion primary round.

title: Google $1.8B Backstop of Fluidstack Leases at TeraWulf Lake Mariner for ~8% Warrants (Upsized to ~$3.2B / ~14%)
description: TeraWulf signed two 10-year HPC colocation leases (CB-3/CB-4) with AI cloud platform Fluidstack at its Lake Mariner campus in Western New York, delivering 200+ MW of critical IT load (~250 MW gross) for ~$3.7B of contracted revenue over the initial term (~$8.7B with two five-year extensions). To support the buildout and its project-related debt financing, Google LLC backstops $1.8B of Fluidstack’s lease obligations under Recognition Agreements among Akela Data LLC, Fluidstack USA I and Google, receiving warrants for 41,011,803 TeraWulf shares at $0.01 exercise (~8% pro forma equity), pledged to project lenders until the backstop becomes effective at lease commencement. On August 18, 2025 Fluidstack exercised its CB-5 option for an incremental 160 MW (~$3.0B more contracted revenue); with an added $1.4B backstop and 32,568,197 incremental warrants, Google’s cumulative backstop rose to ~$3.2B and its pro forma warrant position to ~14% of TeraWulf equity.

title: OpenAI $8.3 Billion Tranche at $300B Valuation Led by Dragoneer
description: OpenAI secured $8.3 billion at a $300 billion valuation as part of its $40 billion 2025 fundraise, led by Dragoneer Investment Group with a $2.8 billion check alongside Blackstone, TPG, T. Rowe Price, Sequoia, Andreessen Horowitz and others, closing months ahead of schedule amid fivefold oversubscription.

title: OpenAI-Oracle 4.5 GW Stargate Capacity Expansion
description: OpenAI and Oracle agreed to develop 4.5 GW of additional Stargate data center capacity running on over two million chips, bringing total Stargate capacity under development past 5 GW. Neither party disclosed a dollar contract value, so no cash figure is recorded.

title: OpenAI Adds Google Cloud as Compute Partner (Reported Deal, Terms Undisclosed)
description: Reuters and CNBC reported on July 16, 2025 that OpenAI had signed a deal to use Google Cloud’s computing capacity for parts of its AI workloads, with Reuters listing Google Cloud as an OpenAI partner amid growing demand for computing capacity; reporting indicated the agreement was finalized in May 2025. Neither OpenAI nor Google issued a formal announcement and no financial terms, duration or capacity figures were disclosed. The arrangement marks OpenAI’s further diversification beyond its founding Microsoft relationship and beyond the AWS platform agreement recorded at deal ...074, at a time of persistent compute shortages.

title: Google and Brookfield Hydro Framework Agreement (up to 3 GW; $3B+ Initial 670 MW PPAs)
description: Google and Brookfield signed a first-of-its-kind Hydro Framework Agreement to deliver up to 3,000 MW of carbon-free hydroelectric capacity across the United States. The first contracts executed under the framework are two 20-year power purchase agreements for Brookfield’s Holtwood and Safe Harbor facilities in Pennsylvania (670 MW, more than $3 billion), supporting relicensing, upgrades, and Google’s 24/7 carbon-free energy goal in PJM with expansion envisaged into MISO.

title: Thinking Machines Lab $2 Billion Seed Round at $12B Valuation
description: Thinking Machines Lab closed a $2 billion a16z-led seed round at a $12 billion valuation with NVIDIA, Accel, ServiceNow, Cisco, AMD and Jane Street participating, one of the largest seed rounds on record.

title: Google Licenses Windsurf Agentic Coding Tech and Hires CEO for ~$2.4 Billion
description: On July 11, 2025 Alphabet’s Google announced a ~$2.4 billion payment covering a non-exclusive license to Windsurf’s agentic-coding technology and a talent package bringing co-founder/CEO Varun Mohan, co-founder Douglas Chen and key R&D staff into Google DeepMind. Windsurf was not acquired by Google, which took no equity; days later the remaining company, IP and brand were sold to Cognition after OpenAI’s ~$3 billion acquisition talks had collapsed earlier in the spring, partly amid friction with Microsoft.

title: Meta Acquires Voice-AI Startup PlayAI; Entire Team Joins Meta Superintelligence Labs
description: Meta completed its acquisition of PlayAI, the voice-AI startup behind human-sounding voice generation, voice cloning and conversational voice agents, first reported as a completed deal by Bloomberg on July 11, 2025 and confirmed by a Meta spokesperson. An internal memo said the entire PlayAI team would join Meta the following week, reporting to voice-AI veteran Johan Schalkwyk (who had just joined Meta from Sesame AI after overseeing speech AI research at Google), with PlayAI's "natural voices" work mapped onto Meta AI characters, Meta AI, wearables and audio content creation. Financial terms were not disclosed; the deal continued Meta's mid-2025 superintelligence talent spree (Scale AI/Alexandr Wang, aggressive OpenAI recruiting).

title: CoreWeave's ~$9B All-Stock Acquisition of Core Scientific - Announced July 2025, Rejected by Stockholders and Terminated
description: CoreWeave and Core Scientific signed a definitive agreement on July 7, 2025 under which CoreWeave would acquire Core Scientific in an all-stock transaction: 0.1235 newly issued CoreWeave Class A shares per Core Scientific share, implying a total equity value of approximately $9.0 billion ($20.40 per share, a ~66% premium to the unaffected June 25, 2025 price of $12.30), giving CoreWeave ownership of ~1.3 GW of gross power across Core Scientific's footprint (including ~840 existing gross MW already supporting CoreWeave HPC contracts plus ~500 gross MW of crypto-mining capacity) with 1 GW+ expansion potential, and eliminating over $10 billion of projected 12-year lease overhead. The deal was expected to close in Q4 2025, but activist holder Two Seas Capital (~6.2%, its largest active shareholder) campaigned against the fixed, uncollared exchange-ratio structure and valuation, ISS and Glass Lewis recommended voting no, and on October 30, 2025 Core Scientific stockholders failed to approve the merger - casting 20,752,327 votes for versus 203,451,498 against (with 21,588,639 abstentions) - the rare large AI-era deal killed by a target-side shareholder vote. Pursuant to the merger agreement, Core Scientific terminated it effective immediately the same day; no termination fee was payable by Core Scientific for a pure vote-failure termination; and the company remains independent and Nasdaq-listed (CORZ).
